summary: The candidate captures most of the paper's principal degree-theoretic and vector-field results, including the Hopf degree theorem, degree-zero null-homotopy, extension results, Poincare-Hopf, the Euler-characteristic criterion, and the sphere homotopy-group consequence. It is nevertheless weakened by several mathematically inaccurate or underspecified statements, incomplete versions of some gold entries, inconsistent locators, and substantial duplication. The most serious factual error is the claimed formula chi(T^k)=-2(k-2), whereas every torus T^k has Euler characteristic zero.
strengths: Captures the central Hopf degree theorem with the correct equivalence between homotopy and equality of degrees.
Includes most foundational degree and winding-number infrastructure, including local orientation signs and the signed-preimage formula.
Covers the main vector-field chain: finite-zero perturbation, zero removal when the index sum vanishes, the Euler-characteristic criterion, Poincare-Hopf, and a hairy-ball consequence.
Marks Sard, isotopy, transversality, epsilon-neighborhood, and Poincare-Hopf results as external.
Most displayed formulas have balanced LaTeX delimiters and remain mathematically readable.
issues: The Euler-characteristic calculation incorrectly states chi(T^k)=-2(k-2); the gold reference correctly gives chi(T^k)=0.

The epsilon-neighborhood theorem has the wrong quantifier: it is stated for an arbitrary epsilon>0 instead of asserting the existence of a sufficiently small epsilon, and its geometric conclusion is incomplete.

The stereographic-identification entry incorrectly describes pi_s^{-1}: R^{k+1}\setminus{0} -> S^k as stereographic projection; the relevant map from punctured Euclidean space to the sphere is radial normalization, while stereographic projection identifies S^k minus a point with R^k.
The vector-field index definition is absent, even though index is subsequently used in several extracted claims.
The S^1 base case is reduced to the degree-zero case and omits the full equal-degree classification and the standard representative z -> z^n.
The hairy-ball entry only states the S^2 case, omitting the gold result for every even-dimensional sphere S^{2m}.

Several cited background theorems are recorded only as descriptions of how the proof invokes them rather than as properly delimited theorem statements, notably Sard and the two transversality results.

There is considerable redundant extraction: degree-zero sphere maps, zero-winding punctured-space maps, degree classification, isotopy, finite-zero vector fields, and vector-field zero removal each appear more than once.
Some page locators disagree with the gold reference, including degree-zero null-homotopy, the extension theorem, the vector-field Euler criterion, and Poincare-Hopf.
External attribution is usually limited to the theorem name and omits the literature reference supplied by the gold artifact.
Several extra entries are proof steps, constructions, or prose observations classified as standalone definitions or theorems, producing avoidable fragmentation.

entryLevelComparison.assessment: The core equal-degree classification is correctly captured, though the candidate states a more general domain than the gold entry.
Mathematically equivalent statement, but it is duplicated and its page differs from the gold locator.
Captures a degree-zero extension criterion, but uses a generalized manifold formulation rather than the gold sphere-to-disk formulation and has a different page locator.
No standalone definition of the index of an isolated vector-field zero was extracted.
The sphere values are correct, but the torus formula is false; chi(T^k)=0.
Recognizes the cited theorem and nearest-point map, but incorrectly quantifies epsilon and omits the sufficiently-small tubular-neighborhood condition.
Only the degree-zero special case is present; the complete classification and z -> z^n representative are missing.
Correctly identifies an external invocation, but does not extract the full theorem that regular values form a dense full-measure set.
The main equivalence is captured accurately, with somewhat stronger orientation and connectedness hypotheses than the gold entry.
Correct for S^2 but incomplete relative to the all-even-dimensional-spheres statement in the gold reference.
Correctly records pi_k(S^k) isomorphic to Z and classification by degree.
